title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on intermittent timeouts and 5xx errors observed during last week's pilot load test; discussed root-cause hypotheses (prefix cache eviction, autoscaler config, rate limiting), short-term mitigations (retry backoff, increase burst capacity, temporary routing to Hosted), and agreed next steps for on-prem telemetry, adjusted autoscaler thresholds, and a targeted load-run on Friday.
next_steps: Redwood to share filtered logs and error-rate dashboard (Aaron) by 2026-05-14
Customer to provide pod-level metrics + VPC flow logs (Marcus) by 2026-05-15
Run targeted 10k req/hr load test on Friday with new autoscaler settings (Samira/Aaron)
Follow-up call to review results and finalize canary traffic plan on Monday 2026-05-18
action_items: Aaron Mitchell: export and share filtered 5xx trace logs + s3 link (due 2026-05-14)
Marcus Ng: provide pod CPU/memory + VPC flow log slice for the incident window (due 2026-05-15)
Samira Lee: propose autoscaler tuning (min replicas, surge, cooldown) and retry/backoff defaults (due 2026-05-14)
Lena Ortiz: confirm stakeholder availability for Friday load-run and Monday follow-up (due 2026-05-14)
transcript:
[00:00] Aaron (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through the incident followup from the load test last week, talk root causes and actions. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Jaya (Customer): Jaya here, hi. Marcus here as well.
[00:16] Marcus (Customer): Yep Marcus, good morning.
[00:20] Samira (SE): Samira from Redwood. I took a first pass at the logs overnight. There are a couple of patterns I wanna call out.
[00:30] Jaya: Great, yeah we saw a spike of 5xxs at about 10:23am last Tuesday, about a 4 minute window where error rate climbed to ~6%. Timeouts and 5xxs, mostly 504 and some 502.
[00:45] Aaron: Right, and the client reported rate-limited responses too -- some 429s at the front, and then downstream 5xx when the requests routed to the dedicated pool.
[00:58] Samira: Exactly. My working hypothesis is a combination: autoscaler lag + cache eviction for large conversation prefixes. When KV cache misses happen under load we see CPU spikes, slow tail latency, and some worker OOM/restarts in the dedicated pods.
[01:18] Marcus: We didn't see OOMs on our side though, our node metrics looked fine, but we did see CPU stochastic spikes. It's possible the per-pod queueing reached a limit and the runtime returned 502s.
[01:30] Jaya: Also worth noting we were pushing longer sequences for the experiment — average ctx ~2,200 tokens — so that likely increased memory pressure on the model variant, and the quantized variant we used was new in the catalog.
[01:46] Samira: Right, and a couple of things in the logs: a) lots of "kv_cache_miss" markers, b) increasing tail latency in the 95-99th which aligns with the errors. c) rate-limit backpressure in the edge layer — some requests dropped early as 429s.
[02:05] Aaron: Okay so how do we prioritize fixes? Short-term mitigation options: increase reserved burst capacity for your dedicated pool, temporarily route a fraction of traffic to Hosted to absorb peaks, or modify client retry/backoff to be more conservative.
[02:25] Marcus: Temporarily routing to Hosted is doable but we have PCI-like compliance concerns; need to confirm with security. We prefer staying on Dedicated but we need reliability.
[02:36] Lena (PM): From product's POV the biggest risk is user-facing errors during business hours. We need a solution that doesn't require long infra changes.
[02:47] Samira: For immediate relief I'd recommend: bump min_replicas by 30% for the next 48h, increase burst capacity, and turn on sticky prefix caching (we can enable a more aggressive cache TTL for your workloads). That should lower kv miss rate.
[03:03] Jaya: Aggressive cache TTL sounds good. Any risk of returning stale semantics? Our app is mostly read/assist style so should be fine.
[03:10] Samira: Yep, should be safe. We can also change the retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, starting at 200ms, max 2s, and cap retries to 3. Right now I saw some fast retries which amplify the spike.
[03:25] Aaron: There's also the question of the autoscaler settings — current cooldown is 120s, min_replicas is 2, max 10. With the load pattern we hit the scale-up path too slowly. Proposed: min 3, cooldown 60s, scale-step 2.
[03:42] Marcus: That makes sense. Any concerns about cost? We need to balance.
[03:46] Aaron: Short-term cost bump is limited — it's a temporary play to stabilize. Long-term we'll tune model variant or sequence trimming.
[03:54] Jaya: Quick question on the 429s: are they being applied globally or per-customer? We saw some 429s for other tenants in the logs — could be noisy neighbors.
[04:05] Samira: At the edge it's per-route but the routing policy can fall back to shared capacity if dedicated is saturated. It looked like fallbacks triggered and then the shared pool throttled, hence some 429s.
[04:18] Aaron: We've seen situations where fallback to shared created a feedback loop — too many fallbacks cause shared throttling which then cascades.
[04:25] Marcus: Ugh. Is there a way to gate fallbacks so it doesn't cascade?
[04:30] Samira: Yes — we can restrict fallback bandwidth per-customer, or set a hard cap on fallback requests. That way we fail fast rather than pile onto shared.
[04:40] Lena: Ok actionables — we need logs and a replay window to correlate. Marcus can you get us the pod-level metrics and VPC flow logs?
[04:49] Marcus: Yes I can pull that. It might take a day to sanitize and share.
[04:53] Aaron: We'll also share filtered Redwood runtime traces with 5xx markers and kv cache events. I'll attach a link to the support ticket.
[05:00] Samira: On the telemetry side, please enable the per-request trace flag for the next test run so we can see KV hits/misses and exact kernel timings. That will add a bit of overhead but it's necessary for root cause.
[05:13] Jaya: Ok let's do that for the Friday test. Friday we're planning a 10k req/hr ramp over 30 minutes.
[05:21] Samira: Sounds good — we'll prepare autoscaler param changes and a runbook for the load test.
[05:26] Aaron: Quick note — we saw one worker restart that coincided with a model compilation log line. Could be a kernel selection path that regresses under long contexts. We'll flag the model team too.
[05:39] Marcus: If it's kernel selection, would that be an issue unique to the quantized build? We only switched to quantized to save cost.
[05:46] Samira: Possibly. We'll surface that. In parallel we can try a higher-capacity non-quantized variant for the run to see if errors vanish.
[05:55] Jaya: Ok can you run an A/B during Friday's test? Half traffic on quantized variant, half on non-quantized?
[06:02] Aaron: Yes, we can route a canary percent. We'll need to coordinate exact weights and ensure the experiment won't violate data residency — the non-quantized variant would still be in your Dedicated pool.
[06:14] Lena: What's the expected timeline for the logs and the autoscaler proposal?
[06:18] Aaron: We'll get the logs to you by tomorrow EOD (Aaron). Samira will post the autoscaler + retry changes as a PR to the pilot runbook by tomorrow. Marcus will try to share sanitized metrics by Friday morning.
[06:31] Marcus: I'll prioritize that. One more thing — the client side reported some TLS handshake failures during the spike. Could that be network related?
[06:41] Samira: TLS failures could be a symptom of overloaded edge proxies; we should check the edge TLS metrics and VPC flow logs. We'll add that to the log slice request.
[06:51] Jaya: Also, we had slightly different behavior when requests were routed between AZs. Could be cross-AZ latency.
[06:58] Aaron: Good catch — we'll include AZ tags in the trace slice.
[07:03] Samira: Alright, going to recap: 1) Redwood to share filtered traces/logs; 2) Redwood to propose autoscaler/retry changes; 3) Customer to share pod/VPC logs; 4) Run Friday load test with per-request tracing and A/B model variants; 5) Follow-up Monday to review.
[07:22] Lena: That sounds right. Anything else on compliance or security?
[07:27] Aaron: Marcus flagged PCI-like concerns about routing to Hosted. We should surface the security deck and confirm whether temporary routing is allowable — but prefer to keep things in Dedicated.
[07:37] Jaya: We'll check with security but try to avoid Hosted for now.
[07:40] Aaron: Ok, last thing — I'll also share the error-rate dashboard filter and a short note on how retry amplification can make spikes worse.
[07:49] Jaya: Thanks, appreciated.
[07:52] Aaron: Cool. Meeting adjourned. We'll send notes and links in the support ticket and set up the Monday follow-up.
